h1: The 7 Best Printers Without Ink Subscriptions of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 printers with no ink subscription, scored on refill cost, features and fit, from Epson EcoTank tanks to Brother lasers.
summary: The Epson EcoTank ET-3850 is the best all-round pick: a refillable tank, an automatic document feeder and Ethernet, with no subscription to join. On a budget, the EcoTank ET-2800 does the same ink-tank trick for less. If you print mostly black text, the Brother DCP-L2640DW laser is the lower-maintenance route. For colour documents without a plan, the Brother HL-L3220CDW is the laser to buy.
intro: Ink subscriptions sell a printer at a low price and then bill you monthly for pages you may or may not print. The catch is that some plans keep charging, or stop the printer working with regular cartridges, if you cancel.

The cleanest way out is a printer that has no subscription to begin with. We reviewed seven models across three types: refillable ink tanks, laser printers and a large-cartridge inkjet, and ranked them on how fully they avoid recurring charges, what you get for the money, and who each one suits.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-3850 Wireless Color All-in-One
products.verdict: Refillable tanks, an automatic document feeder and Ethernet. Office features with no ink plan.
products.description:
The ET-3850 is Epson's higher-end EcoTank, with a refillable cartridge-free tank system, an automatic document feeder and both Ethernet and wireless connectivity. There is no cartridge to subscribe against, so the question of a recurring ink plan never comes up.

It beats the cheaper EcoTanks below because the feeder and wired network port turn it into a proper home office machine. Scanning a multi-page contract without lifting the lid every sheet is a real time saver. It also ships with a bonus bottle of black ink. What you pay for is a higher purchase price than the ET-2800 and ET-2400.

Buy it if you scan or copy regularly and want one printer that handles a small office.
cons: Higher upfront price than other EcoTanks
Bigger body than the entry models
products.idealFor: Home offices that scan and copy multi-page documents.
products.skipIf: You print only occasionally and want the cheapest tank printer.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-4800 Wireless All-in-One
products.verdict: Same subscription-free tank base with a feeder, Ethernet and a built-in fax.
products.description:
The ET-4800 sits on the same refillable ink tank foundation as the ET-3850 and adds fax to the feeder and Ethernet. For a home office that still has to send the occasional fax to a clinic or agency, that built-in line saves buying a second device.

It ranks second because fax is a niche need in 2026 and the ET-3850 has the same practical features for most people, plus the bonus ink. If fax is not on your list, the extra capability is wasted. If it is, nothing else here does it.

Choose it if you still deal with faxed forms and want everything in one subscription-free machine.
cons: Fax is niche for most buyers
products.idealFor: Small offices that still send occasional faxes.
products.skipIf: You never fax and would rather save the money.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-2800 Wireless Color All-in-One
products.verdict: The simplest way to dodge ink plans: a wireless tank printer with bottled refills.
products.description:
The ET-2800 swaps cartridges for refillable tanks and adds wireless printing, scanning and copying. You pour in bottled ink when the tanks run low, so there is no cartridge programme that could lock you into a subscription.

It trades the feeder and Ethernet of the ET-3850 for a lower price and a smaller footprint. That makes sense for a student or a household that prints schoolwork and the odd photo, and less sense for anyone scanning stacks of paper.

Best for light to moderate home printing where you want to forget about subscriptions and keep costs down.
products.idealFor: Students and light home users who want zero ink plans.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-2400 Wireless Color All-in-One
products.verdict: A step below the ET-2800 in price with the same subscription-free tank design.
products.description:
The ET-2400 is aimed at everyday home printing and costs less than the ET-2800 and uses the same refillable tank design. Print, scan and copy are all covered over wireless.

It ranks just under the ET-2800 because the two are close, and the ET-2800 is the more established listing. The ET-2400 wins on price, which is why it exists. If the saving matters more to you than the small differences, it is the sensible buy.

This is for households that print regularly but have no need for networking or feeder features.
pros: No ink subscription to opt into
cons: Close to the ET-2800 in capability
products.idealFor: Families who print every week and want the lowest tank price.
products.skipIf: You need a feeder or wired network.

products.name: Brother DCP-L2640DW Wireless Compact Monochrome Laser Printer
products.verdict: Black-and-white laser with duplex and a 250-sheet tray. Its Refresh plan is optional.
products.description:
The DCP-L2640DW is a compact monochrome laser with automatic duplex printing, a 250-sheet paper tray and wireless plus mobile printing. The listing includes a Refresh Subscription trial, but enrolling is optional and standard toner cartridges bought separately work without it.

It differs from the EcoTanks because toner outlasts inkjet ink when you print infrequently. Ink can dry out in a printer left idle, while toner does not, so it suits the person who prints a handful of pages a month. The compromise is no colour at all.

Pick it for text documents and forms, especially if the printer sits unused for weeks at a time.
cons: Listing includes a trial offer to ignore
products.idealFor: People who print mostly text and print rarely.
products.skipIf: You need colour pages or photos.

products.name: Brother HL-L3220CDW Wireless Color Laser Printer
products.verdict: A colour laser with duplex and no bundled plan. Toner is bought only as needed.
products.description:
The HL-L3220CDW is a colour laser rated at 19 pages per minute with a 250-sheet tray and duplex printing. Its listing pushes no bundled subscription, and each toner cartridge is replaced separately, so a recurring plan never enters the picture.

It costs more to run per colour page than a tank printer, which is why it ranks below the EcoTanks. But for anyone who wants sharp colour documents and a machine that does not clog from sitting idle, it is the straightforward choice. It is print-only; the other Brother here handles scanning.

Choose it if you want colour laser output for reports and handouts at a modest volume.
products.idealFor: Colour reports and handouts at modest volumes.

products.name: Brother INKvestment MCF-J5010DW Wireless Color Inkjet All-in-One
products.verdict: Big INKvestment cartridges and a touchscreen. Less subscription-free than a tank, but no plan bundled.
products.description:
The MCF-J5010DW uses larger INKvestment cartridges to cut the number of replacements, includes a 2.7 inch colour touchscreen and prints automatically on both sides. The listing does not bundle a recurring plan.

It is the least subscription-proof entry here because it is still a cartridge-based printer, so you are exposed to cartridge pricing in a way tank owners are not. That is why it ranks last. Where it wins is convenience: the touchscreen and automatic scanning and copying make it easy to use.

Pick it if you prefer cartridges to refilling bottles and want a polished all-in-one.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want cartridges and an easy interface.
products.skipIf: You want to avoid cartridge pricing entirely.

whatMatters.detail: A tank printer is refilled from a bottle, a cartridge printer swaps a sealed unit and a laser uses toner powder. Tanks cost the least per page, lasers hold up best when idle. Check the product title for the words EcoTank, cartridge or laser before you order.

Some listings include a free trial of a manufacturer subscription that can tie ink supply to a plan. An optional trial is fine, but check that regular cartridges still work without it. Look for any mention of enrollment or a monthly plan in the bullets.
If you print under 100 pages a month, a laser stays ready without clogging. If you print more or in colour, a tank usually costs far less per page. Estimate your monthly pages before choosing.
A flatbed-only printer makes scanning stacks of paper slow. An automatic document feeder and Ethernet help in a home office. Look for ADF and Ethernet in the spec bullets.
Automatic duplex saves paper on long documents. Some models in this guide include it, others do not. Check the listing for automatic 2-sided printing, not only manual duplex.

faq.a: A plan bills monthly whether or not you print, and some can limit which cartridges work if you cancel. A tank or laser printer lets you buy ink or toner only when you need it.

faq.q: Is the Brother Refresh Subscription mandatory?
faq.a: On the DCP-L2640DW listing it is an optional trial. Standard toner cartridges bought separately work without enrolling. Check that your listing makes the same distinction before buying.

faq.q: Is an EcoTank worth it over a cheaper cartridge printer?
faq.a: If you print more than occasionally, yes. Refillable tanks avoid cartridge pricing, and the ET-2800 or ET-2400 are priced close to many cartridge printers.

faq.q: Can an EcoTank dry out if I rarely print?
faq.a: Any inkjet can clog if left idle for months. Print a test page every few weeks. If you print rarely, a laser like the Brother DCP-L2640DW is the safer choice.

faq.q: Do I need the ADF on the ET-3850?
faq.a: Only if you scan multi-page documents. For single sheets, a flatbed model like the ET-2800 is fine. The feeder saves lifting the lid on every page.
Tank printers generally cost least per colour page. For black-only text at low volume, a laser can be competitive because toner does not go stale.

finalTake: For most people the Epson EcoTank ET-3850 is the best buy: tank refills, a feeder and Ethernet with nothing to subscribe to. On a budget, the EcoTank ET-2800 keeps the same advantage. If you print rarely and only text, the Brother DCP-L2640DW laser is the low-maintenance choice. And for colour documents without a plan, the Brother HL-L3220CDW is the one.
